idiom_name: QStyledItemDelegate (or a custom QAbstractItemDelegate) paints items; the model owns data and interaction state
implementation_notes: Qt's model/view architecture is the framework's version of the split: the model holds the data and the interaction state and the view asks a delegate to render each item, so the consumer subclasses QStyledItemDelegate and decides how the data looks while the model keeps the behaviour - the documentation recommends QStyledItemDelegate as the base class when implementing custom delegates because it uses the current style to paint. What replaces prop getters is the delegate's paint() receiving the QStyleOptionViewItem and QModelIndex the framework assembled for it, plus the ordinary Qt signal/slot wiring for events; keep the invariant (selection, validation) in the model so every delegate - including Qt's default one - obeys it.
pitfalls: Model indexes are temporary references and should not be stored; use QPersistentModelIndex when a delegate must remember an item across model changes.
A delegate set with setItemDelegate is owned by the view (or must be parented): one created without an owner leaks, and one destroyed while attached leaves a dangling pointer.
paint() runs for many items per frame, so it must stay cheap - no allocation, no I/O, no global state.

variants.name: Framework-free: state owner plus a std::function render callback
variants.idiom_name: state owner + std::function<R(const State&)> render hook
variants.implementation_notes: Outside Qt the pattern is compiled by hand: the behaviour class owns the state and exposes a render hook taking std::function (or a virtual paint hook), so the consumer's lambda decides the markup while the class keeps the transitions - std::function is the general-purpose polymorphic function wrapper that stores lambdas and function objects, which is what a render prop is in C++. Choose this variant when the codebase has no Qt; it is also the better testable core, because the state machine can be exercised with a recording callback instead of a GUI.
pitfalls: std::function type-erases the callback; capturing references to locals that die before view() runs is the classic dangling-lambda bug.
Recursion through the callback (view -> toggle -> view) re-enters the object; emit events or document that view() must not be re-entrant.
Copying the behaviour object copies the callback; if the callback already captured this, the copy points at the original.
